name: eleusis
title: Eleusis
description: Inductive-reasoning card game. Seat 0 is the rule-maker: it writes a secret rule (one restricted Python expression over `card` and `prev`) deciding which card may follow which. The rule must pass a fairness gate (accept rate within [accept_rate_min, accept_rate_max], every card playable after some card, no dead ends) or the rule-maker retries; after rule_retries failures a library rule is used and the rule-maker scores 0. Every other seat is a scientist at its own table (identical deal, same secret rule, no visibility of other tables). Each turn a scientist either plays a card from its hand (the engine says accepted -> mainline, or rejected -> sideline) or guesses the rule as words + code. A guess is correct iff its code agrees with the secret rule on all 2,704 (card, prev) pairs of one deck. A solved scientist scores max(0, max_turns - turns_used - wrong_guess_penalty * wrong_guesses); unsolved scores 0. The rule-maker scores the second-best scientist score.

action.description: Rule-maker: {words, code}. Scientist: {action: 'play', card: 'QD'} or {action: 'guess', words, code}. May be wrapped as {submission: ...}; submission -1 is the harness forfeit signal.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

actTimeout.description: Seconds per agent action. Matches the core harness LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT budget so the framework never kills a seat the harness still considers in flight.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

max_turns.description: Turns per scientist. Every play, guess, or failed action uses one turn.

hand_size.description: Cards in each scientist's hand. After every play one card is drawn, so the hand stays full.

num_decks.description: Standard 52-card decks shuffled together into each table's shoe.

wrong_guess_penalty.description: Points deducted per wrong guess from a solved scientist's score (on top of the turn the guess uses). Run with a low (2) and a high (5) setting to separate bold from cautious play.

rule_retries.description: Rule submissions the rule-maker gets. After this many invalid or unfair rules, a random library rule is used and the rule-maker scores 0.

accept_rate_min.description: Fairness gate: minimum fraction of the 2,704 (card, prev) pairs the rule must accept.

accept_rate_max.description: Fairness gate: maximum fraction of the 2,704 (card, prev) pairs the rule must accept.

seed.description: Seed for the shuffle and fallback-rule choice. Null for nondeterministic play.

freeForm.description: Always true: rules and guesses are open-ended text, so the core harness accepts free-form submissions.

illegalMoveForfeit.description: If true, a model that never produces a valid answer after all harness retries submits -1 instead of raising. The engine scores that as a pass for a scientist (turn used, wrong guess if it was a guess) and a failed rule attempt for the rule-maker, rather than voiding the episode.

savePrompt.description: If disabled, skip logging LLM prompts in the replay file.

saveResponse.description: If disabled, skip logging raw LLM responses in the replay file.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

phase.description: 'rule' (rule-maker writing), 'play' (scientists playing), or 'done'. Empty before initialization.

rule_attempts.description: Rule-maker only: rejected submissions so far, each {words, code, error}.

secret_rule.description: Rule-maker only: the rule in play once accepted, {words, code, source ('rule_maker' or 'library'), accept_rate}. Null before. Scientists never see it.

hand.description: Scientist only: cards in hand, e.g. ['10H', 'QD'] (ranks A, 2-10, J, Q, K; suits S, H, D, C).

mainline.description: Scientist only: accepted cards in order, each {card, rejected} where rejected lists the cards refused directly after it.

wrong_guesses.description: Scientist only: incorrect guesses so far, each {words, code, error}; error is set when the code did not compile.

log.description: Scientist only: one entry per used turn: {turn, type: 'play'|'guess'|'pass', ...}.

turns_used.description: Scientist only: turns used so far.

solved.description: Scientist only: true once a guess was correct.

score.description: Scientist only: final score once solved; 0 otherwise.

reward.description: Scientist: its score. Rule-maker: the second-best scientist score (0 if a library rule had to be used).

call_details.prompt:
You are the RULE-MAKER in Eleusis, a game about discovering a hidden rule.

You write a secret rule deciding which card may be played after which. 2 scientists then try to discover it, each at its own table. Each turn a scientist either plays a card from its hand (your rule decides whether it is accepted after the last accepted card) or guesses your rule. A guess is correct only if its code gives the same answer as yours on every (card, prev) pair of a 52-card deck. Each scientist has 30 turns.

Scoring:
- A scientist that solves your rule scores max(0, 30 - turns used - 2 x wrong guesses); otherwise 0.
- You score the LOWER of the two (so you score only if both scientists solve it) scientist score.
- After 3 rejected rules, a random built-in rule is used instead and you score 0.

Rule language: ONE Python expression that is true when `card` may be played after `prev`.
- card.rank, prev.rank: 1-13 (A=1, J=11, Q=12, K=13)
- card.suit, prev.suit: 'S', 'H', 'D', 'C'
- card.color, prev.color: 'red' (H, D) or 'black' (S, C)
Allowed: integer and string constants; == != < <= > >=; `in` / `not in` with a tuple such as (2, 3, 5); and, or, not; + - * // % on numbers; `x if condition else y`; abs(...).
Nothing else: no other names, functions, attributes, indexing, loops or lambdas. Use single quotes inside code.
Example of the syntax: abs(card.rank - prev.rank) <= 2 and card.suit != prev.suit

Fairness check, run on all 52 x 52 = 2,704 ordered (card, prev) pairs. Your rule is rejected unless:
1. it accepts between 20% and 60% of the pairs;
2. every card can be played after at least one card;
3. after every card, at least one card can be played.


Think it through, then end your reply with one JSON object:
```json
{"words": "<the rule in plain English>", "code": "<one expression>"}
```
For example: {"words": "Rank within 2 of the previous rank and a different suit", "code": "abs(card.rank - prev.rank) <= 2 and card.suit != prev.suit"}
